newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Clinton still ponders successor for Christopher.
newsitem.headline: Clinton still ponders successor for Christopher.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher said on Saturday he did not know who his successor would be and that a decision might not be made until the end of the year.

Asked at an APEC news conference who would succeed him, Christopher said: "I do not know who my successor will be. President (Bill) Clinton is reflecting on the subject. I expect he will decide sometime between now and the end of the year."

Christopher, 71, submitted his resignation immediately after Clinton was re-elected for a second term as president early this month. Clinton will be sworn in and is expected to have his cabinet in place by January 20.
The secretary of state also reassured the other 17 Pacific Rim members of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum that his successor would continue to play an important role in Asia.
"I think I can assure you that my successor will reflect the president's determination that the United States play a very important role in APEC and other Asia-Pacific organisations.

"One of the hallmarks, one of the signatures of President Clinton's first four years has been an emphasis on Asia, reflecting the importance Asia has to the United States in many ways, economically, politically and environmentally," Christopher said.
Clinton, who hosted the first APEC summit in Seattle in 1993, will attend the 1996 summit at the former U.S. naval base of Subic Bay north of Manila on Monday.
